about: FREIGHTIX story archive. Written by website-v4/build.py; read by network-watch/stories.py.

versions.headline: Victorian election puts toll caps and road spending on the table
versions.summary: Toll caps and road spending are the big freight issues in the Victorian election. Costings for the road plans are out.
versions.who: Carriers paying Victorian tolls and anyone running Victorian roads.
versions.story: Freight issues in the Victorian election centre on toll caps and road spending. Election costings set out each side's road spending plans. Our data does not give the toll cap amounts or which projects get funded.
versions.impact: A toll cap would change the cost of runs that use Victorian toll roads. Fleet owners should read the costings and be ready to reprice contracts if tolls change.

versions.headline: $140.8 million plan to flood proof an interstate freight route
versions.summary: A $140.8 million plan aims to flood proof a major interstate freight route.
versions.who: Linehaul operators who lose runs when that route floods.
versions.story: A $140.8 million plan aims to flood proof a major interstate freight route. Our data does not name the route. A concept design for a $141 million Newell Highway upgrade also came out yesterday. The figures are close, but our data does not say if they are the same project. The news lands while floods have the Calder shut in three places.
versions.impact: Flood closures cost carriers hours, as the Calder shows today. Watch for the route and the build timeline before planning around it.

versions.headline: Concept design out for $141 million Newell Highway upgrade
versions.summary: A concept design is out for a $141 million Newell Highway upgrade.
versions.who: Melbourne to Brisbane linehaul and anyone running the Newell.
versions.story: The concept design for a $141 million Newell Highway upgrade has been released. Our data does not say which section it covers or when work starts. The Newell carries the inland Melbourne to Brisbane run.
versions.impact: Newell operators should read the design to see which section it touches. Watch for work dates so you can plan around lane closures.

versions.headline: Queensland changes low loader access to cut permits
versions.summary: Queensland has changed low loader access rules. The aim is to cut permit requirements.
versions.who: Queensland low loader operators and the shippers who book them.
versions.story: Queensland has changed access arrangements for low loaders. The goal is to cut the number of permits operators need. Our data does not list which routes or loads are covered.
versions.impact: Fewer permits could mean less paperwork and quicker bookings for low loader work. Operators should check the new access terms before applying for their next permit.

versions.headline: Fair Work halts Christmas rail freight disruption
versions.summary: Fair Work has stopped a rail freight disruption planned for the Christmas period.
versions.who: Shippers and carriers relying on rail for Christmas freight.
versions.story: Fair Work has stepped in to halt rail freight disruption over Christmas. Our data does not say which operator or which lines were involved. Our data does not give the details of the action either.
versions.impact: Shippers who had planned to move rail freight onto road should check with their rail operator before changing bookings.

versions.headline: TWU warns of fuel and dangerous goods disruptions
versions.summary: The Transport Workers Union has warned of disruptions involving fuel and dangerous goods.
versions.who: Fuel and dangerous goods carriers and their customers.
versions.story: The Transport Workers Union has warned of possible disruptions involving fuel and dangerous goods. Our data does not say what is causing them or when they could start. The national diesel terminal gate price is 230.9 cents a litre, down 35.6 cents in 30 days.
versions.impact: If you carry fuel or dangerous goods, or depend on fuel deliveries, stay in touch with your supplier. Wait for detail before changing plans.

versions.headline: Hino issues voluntary recall over Takata airbags
versions.summary: Hino has issued a voluntary safety recall. The fault is the Takata airbag problem.
versions.who: Fleets and owner drivers running Hino trucks.
versions.story: Hino has issued a voluntary safety recall. It is tied to the Takata airbag issue. Our data does not say which models or build years are covered. Owners should get the detail from Hino or their dealer.
versions.impact: Fleet managers should check every Hino on the books against the recall and book the work in. Plan cover for any unit that goes into the workshop.

versions.headline: Penske Truck Leasing opens in Tasmania
versions.summary: Penske Truck Leasing has launched in Tasmania.
versions.who: Tasmanian operators who lease or hire trucks have another supplier.
versions.story: Penske Truck Leasing has launched in Tasmania. Our data does not give pricing, fleet size or locations. It adds another leasing option in the state.
versions.impact: Tasmanian fleets coming up to a lease renewal have another name to get a quote from. Compare prices before you renew.

versions.headline: Australian truck sales slump to 2017 levels
versions.summary: Truck sales in Australia have fallen back to where they were in 2017.
versions.who: Truck dealers, and fleets deciding when to buy new.
versions.story: Australian truck sales have slumped to 2017 levels. Our data does not include the figures behind the fall or the reasons for it. Watch for the full numbers.
versions.impact: Slow sales may leave dealers keener to deal. Fleets due to replace units could ask for sharper prices, but check the full figures first.

versions.headline: Trucking association election opens a door for small operators
versions.summary: The Australian Trucking Association (ATA) election is giving owner drivers and small fleets a platform.
versions.who: Owner drivers and small fleet owners who want a say in industry policy.
versions.story: The Australian Trucking Association (ATA) is holding an election. It is being seen as a platform for owner drivers and small fleets. Our data does not name the candidates or give the voting dates.
versions.impact: Small operators should find out who is standing and what they back. Your voice at the ATA shapes the policy you end up working under.

versions.headline: Farmers name inflation and diesel as their biggest costs
versions.summary: Inflation and diesel costs top the list of challenges for Australian farmers. The national terminal gate average is 230.9 cents a litre.
versions.who: Carriers hauling for farm customers, who may feel the pressure on rates.
versions.story: Australian farmers rate inflation and diesel as their top challenges. The national average terminal gate price was 230.9 cents a litre on 27 November. That is up 32.2 per cent on 12 months ago. It is down 11.4 cents over 7 days and 35.6 cents over 30 days.
versions.impact: Farm customers under cost pressure may push back on fuel levies. With diesel down 35.6 cents in 30 days, check your levy still matches the price.
